name: Treaty with the Kickapoo, 1809
aka: Treaty of Vincennes with the Kickapoo, December 9, 1809
promises: For the Kickapoo's assent to the Fort Wayne cession, a permanent additional annuity of $400 and $800 in goods (Article 1).
For a further cession between that tract, the Wabash and the Vermilion River, an annuity of $100 and $700 in goods (Article 2).
The Treaty of Greenville's terms on annuity payment and on the Indians' right to hunt on ceded land would apply (Article 3).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found the Kickapoo received $11,500 in value ($1,500 in goods and $500 in annuities commuted at $10,000) for the two tracts ceded under this treaty (Royce Areas 73 and 74, 405,000 and 91,000 acres in the Wabash valley), found them worth $1.40 and $1.50 an acre, held the consideration unconscionable, and found the Kickapoo entitled to $351,750 less the $11,500 credit.

landTaken: Royce Area 73 (405,000 acres) and Royce Area 74 (91,000 acres), straddling the Illinois-Indiana line in the Wabash valley (Docket 99/314-C/317 supplemental findings, 1969). The Wea shared in Area 73 (Fort Wayne treaty and convention of 26 October 1809) and joined the cession of Area 74 in 1818.
compensation: $1,500 in goods and $500 a year in permanent annuities, valued at $11,500. Final award of $340,250 in 1970, with the United States reserving offset claims for gratuities after 2 January 1810.
today: The Commission valued Area 73 as of 5 March 1810, the ratification date of this treaty, and Area 74 as of 7 January 1819, when the Wea consent was ratified.

nationVoice.summary: Chairman Lester Randall told the Senate in 2018 that the United States moved the Tribe several times, from Wisconsin through Illinois and Missouri to Kansas, under nine treaties made between 1809 and 1862, and that today the Tribe holds 4,859 acres in trust and 2,189 acres in fee within its 30 square mile reservation.

openQuestions: The Kappler text gives the proclamation date as 'Mar. 8,' with the year cut off in the OSU page.
A web search for the Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas, Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma and Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas accounts of this treaty found no tribal page; a nation statement is still wanted.
